verdict.rationale: TypeSafe's docs state the data-handling commitment in plain language: Jev is not trained on customer requests or responses, and the docs point to a DPA, a Privacy Policy and zero data retention for enterprise customers. Pricing is published openly, which covers part of the commercial terms. Nothing in the pack documents an acceptable-use or prohibited-uses policy, which is the core 'what I may build' element. missing for 10: a prohibited/acceptable-use policy, commercial terms beyond pricing (output ownership, licensing, terms of service), the actual DPA/privacy text in the pack, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, the usage policy is clear about what I may build — prohibited uses, commercial terms, and data-handling commitments in plain language

citations.quote: Jev is not trained on customer requests or responses. See Legal for the Data Processing Agreement, the Privacy Policy, and details on zero data retention (ZDR) for enterprise customers.
Charged per input token. Output tokens are free.
